cards.explanation: The answer is lying and stealing. The LORD says, “Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant…” (Hosea 4:2). When there's no truth in the land, lying doesn't have to fight for room. It walks right in and takes a seat.
The answer is mourns. The LORD says, “Therefore the land mourns…” (Hosea 4:3). It's a strong picture: the ground itself is in mourning over what's happening on top of it. That's how heavy this is.

The answer is True. In Hosea 4:3, the LORD says all who dwell in the land will waste away with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air. Then He adds that even the fish of the sea disappear. Nobody is left out of that list.

The answer is False. The text doesn't have the prophet staying on his feet. The LORD says the people will stumble by day, and “…the prophet will stumble with you by night…” (Hosea 4:5). The prophet stumbles too.

The answer is as His priests. The LORD says, “Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests.” (Hosea 4:6). Right before that, He says, “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” The rejection comes because they rejected knowledge.

The answer is their children. The LORD says, “Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.” (Hosea 4:6). The weight lands on the next generation. It's a sober line, so I'll just leave it right there.

The answer is a thing of disgrace. The LORD says, “…they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace.” (Hosea 4:7). That's the worst swap I've heard of, friends, and I once got picked up out of a bin for 25 cents. Giving up the Glory for a thing of disgrace is a sad trade.

The answer is False, because it's not only the priests. The LORD says, “And it shall be like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.” (Hosea 4:9). Both the people and the priest are named, so neither one gets skipped.
The answer is False. The LORD says, “They will eat but not be satisfied…” (Hosea 4:10). They eat and they still aren't satisfied. I think that sounds like a heavy thing to live with.

The answer is their understanding. The LORD says promiscuity, wine and new wine “…take away understanding.” (Hosea 4:11). That fits what He said earlier, that His people are destroyed for lack of knowledge (Hosea 4:6). It's a chain, friends: these things take away understanding, and without understanding a people comes to ruin (Hosea 4:14).

The answer is their wooden idols. The LORD says, “My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rods inform them.” (Hosea 4:12). They go to wood for answers. I think that's a sad place to look.

The answer is shade. The LORD says they sacrifice “…under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant.” (Hosea 4:13). Picking a spot because it's comfortable is something I understand, friends, since I wouldn't stand over a hot oven either. Here, though, it's where they chose to sacrifice.

The answer is they will come to ruin. The LORD says, “So a people without understanding will come to ruin.” (Hosea 4:14). It connects to what He said earlier about His people being destroyed for lack of knowledge (Hosea 4:6). No understanding, no footing.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, may Judah avoid such guilt!” (Hosea 4:15). Judah gets a hope, a wish that it stays clear of this guilt. Israel is the one being called out.
The answer is Gilgal and Beth-aven. The warning says, “Do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven…” (Hosea 4:15). Those are the two places named. Joppa and Tarshish aren't in that warning.

The answer is a stubborn heifer. The LORD says, “For Israel is as obstinate as a stubborn heifer.” (Hosea 4:16). Then He asks, “Can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?” A stubborn heifer doesn't follow easy, and that's the picture.
The answer is False. The text says, “Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!” (Hosea 4:17). It doesn't say to go bring him home. It's a hard line, and I'll leave it as it stands.

The answer is shame. The LORD says, “The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.” (Hosea 4:19). The whirlwind and the shame come together in this verse. Shame is the word the LORD uses for what their sacrifices bring.
